output.reason: 45-year-old with 30 minutes of ongoing crushing central chest pressure radiating to the left arm, with diaphoresis and nausea — a presentation sufficiently plausible for acute coronary syndrome to require immediate emergency assessment with ECG and troponin; no remote pathway can substitute.
output.patientMessage: Call 911 now and stay resting until help arrives; do not drive yourself or have someone else drive you. Crushing central chest pressure lasting 30 minutes with left-arm radiation, sweating and nausea can mean a heart attack, which needs immediate emergency testing and treatment. If you become faint, collapse or your symptoms worsen while waiting, tell the 911 dispatcher right away and follow their instructions.
differential: Acute coronary syndrome (STEMI/NSTEMI/unstable angina) — pressure with left-arm radiation, diaphoresis, nausea >20 minutes
Aortic dissection — not excluded; pain character and back/tearing features, pulses and arm pressures unreported
Pulmonary embolism or other serious chest pathology — breathlessness and pleuritic features unreported
